decisions.name: Lemma III.2.12 and Theorem 1 uniformization clause
decisions.reason: Closure of Borel uniformizing functions is not required by the assigned regularity page and would add an unused consumer-facing theorem.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Solovay Part III Lemma 2.12, printed p.52, imports a Borel function into the inner model specifically to establish Theorem 1(5), the almost-everywhere uniformization clause. Read that lemma and its application. The current page proves measurability, Baire property, perfect sets, DC and the named negative consequences, not Theorem 1(5). These regularity contracts do not require the stronger uniformization conclusion; its exclusion stands.

decisions.name: No definable well-ordering of the continuum
decisions.reason: The assigned design consumes Theorem 4.12's ultrafilter/BPI branch, not the preceding continuum-definability result.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Read Feferman scanned printed pp.340–344, including the entire Theorem 4.11 argument and Theorem 4.12. The no-definable-well-ordering result is the delta=1 branch, compatible with AC, whereas the ultrafilter branch uses delta=omega. Current def-feferman-tail-flip-definability-model explicitly defines a different HS presentation and the page uses the tail-complement argument. It does not claim to inherit Theorem 4.11 or identify the two source models. This exclusion stands.

decisions.name: Repický parameter-definable maximal-ideal primeness shortcut
decisions.reason: Its promotion from parameter-definable elements to maximality among parameter-definable ideals has an unresolved definable-witness gap; the page uses the independent Halpern–Lévy search-and-shift construction.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Read all four pages of Repicky, including p.545 promotion from primality for parameter-definable elements to maximality among parameter-definable ideals. The stated definable-witness issue is not resolved merely by an ordinal-definable collection having an element. Current page prose, thm-basic-cohen-model-satisfies-bpi-and-fails-choice Proof 2.1, and the search-and-shift supplier explicitly avoid that shortcut. Excluding the shortcut stands; this is not a claim that the underlying BPI theorem is false.

decisions.name: Omission of the original full Halpern–Läuchli application in favor of the elementary continuity proof
decisions.reason: This is a methodological comparison, not a mathematical result to scaffold; the full partition theorem and the complete elementary Cohen-model proof are both retained separately.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Repicky abstract and introduction explicitly replace the full Halpern–Lauchli argument by an elementary case. That methodological comparison is not itself an additional theorem. However, the current Cohen-model and HL page prose expressly abandon the elementary continuity-to-primality shortcut and retain search-and-shift instead. The row reason saying the complete elementary Cohen proof is retained is stale. Owner must reconcile that description; no mathematical content was added or removed.

decisions.name: Basic Cohen symmetric-model construction
decisions.reason: Already supplied by the published prerequisite page symmetric-extensions-and-basic-choice-failure-models; its statements and proofs were checked rather than duplicated.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: The current published def-basic-cohen-symmetric-system specifies the Cohen forcing, finite permutations, finite supports and HS interpretation; current published cor-basic-cohen-model-fails-well-orderability-and-choice gives the Dedekind-finite obstruction. Read both current files. Jech Chapter 5 is their model background, while its Chapter 7 explicitly does not supply the basic-Cohen BPI proof. The current BPI page consumes the earlier model and separately supplies search-and-shift, so not duplicating the model construction is correct.

decisions.name: Halpern-Lauchli combinatorial route
decisions.reason: The binding design requires the earlier direct Repicky continuity route and forbids making the later Halpern-Lauchli page a prerequisite.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Current boolean-prime-ideal-theorem-in-the-basic-cohen-model prose and lem-basic-cohen-search-and-shift-prime-ideal-construction use the Halpern–Levy search-and-shift route with Ramsey and Erdos–Rado inputs. Repicky is read as the abandoned shortcut, not the required direct proof. The current plan still correctly forbids a dependency on the later HL page, but the reason mandating direct Repicky continuity contradicts the current frozen content. Owner must reconcile the reason and design; no forward edge or replacement proof is introduced here.

decisions.name: Sections III.1.12–1.13: Borel uniformization modulo null or meagre sets
decisions.reason: The assigned design requires regularity and its negative consequences, not almost-everywhere uniformization; no owned consumer needs this stronger theorem.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Solovay Part III §§1.12–1.13 construct a Borel selector outside a null or meagre exceptional set for a definable relation with nonempty sections. Read the exact hypotheses and conclusions. Current regularity items prove measurability/Baire/perfect-set properties and named consequences, without claiming this uniformization theorem. The stronger selector is not required by those selected contracts; exclusion stands.

decisions.name: Consequences for pathological measure and Borel-set behavior
decisions.reason: This pair is confined to collapse layers, countable-union/regularity failures, and ultrafilter principles; measure theory is not a consumer in the design.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Jech printed p.144 states additional measure/Borel consequences after the Feferman–Levy countable-union result. Current SET20 retains the countable union, omega_1/cofinality and ultrafilter failures; the subsequent Solovay page uses its own earlier published measure and descriptive-set suppliers, not those Feferman–Levy pathologies. The excluded consequences are not needed by the selected proof interfaces.

decisions.name: Generalized Feferman constructions and uniformity spectra
decisions.reason: The batch needs only the explicit Blass-attributed ordinal reduction; later spectrum constructions are unrelated.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Hayut–Karagila Spectra of uniformity, introduction and §§3–5, extend the Feferman/Jech constructions and prescribe uniformity spectra. Current thm-blass-model-has-only-principal-ultrafilters uses the earlier least-ordinal/completeness reduction of Proposition 2.3 and Corollary 2.4, not an Easton-like spectrum construction. Those later stronger model constructions remain outside the selected arbitrary-set ultrafilter endpoint.

decisions.name: Applications to strong, Woodin, strongly compact, supercompact and huge cardinals
decisions.reason: The assigned Blass endpoint needs only the measurable-cardinal case.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Hamkins Gap Forcing Corollary 12 is the measurable-cardinal preservation result; Corollaries 13 and 15–18 separately address strong, Woodin, strongly compact, supercompact and huge notions. Current thm-small-forcing-does-not-create-measurable-cardinals is the measurable specialization used by the Blass argument. The stronger cardinal applications are not assumed there. Their exclusion stands.

decisions.name: Relationships among UF(omega), BPI(omega), and ultrafilters on Russell sets
decisions.reason: These comparison principles are not required by the assigned SET20 inventory; only the explicit Blass-model witness and its tail symmetry are retained.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Tachtsis abstract and §1 state the comparisons between UF(omega), BPI(omega) and free ultrafilters on Russell sets. Current SET20 retains its explicit paired finite-modification Russell witness and the principal-ultrafilter endpoint, not the separate implication diagram. Those comparisons are not inputs to the retained tail-symmetry proof, so exclusion stands.
